source_language_scope: Supplied English records only; no new Greek, Hebrew or critical-apparatus verification.
numbering: Exact original nested chapter/verse order, references and anchors retained. The actual inventory contains 723 units in 25 chapters; continuation units and numeric gaps are recorded in inventory.json.
method: Read complete actual source and retained target passages with necessary context; reread every particular explanation before completing its initial curated pass. The full source inventory preceded review and earned zero review credit.
completion_definition: Completed means the initial curated cross-reference pass: the source verse and every listed target passage were read in the pinned Saints-Translation English records, and each retained pair has a specific explanation. It does not mean every possible biblical connection has been exhausted, or independent scholarly approval.
canon_policy: Old Testament cross-references exclusively within the Saints Holy Bible 70-book edition: 43 source books in their exact order and divisions; matching targets restricted to its 70 books.

unresolved_candidates.status: pending proposed family-comparison equivalence; no reconciliation credit
unresolved_candidates.reason: The complete continuation compares Jehoram with his brothers and mother; the main notice compares him with father and mother. The retained partial comparison concerns the explicit evil assessment and maternal qualification only. The reverse3:2/1:18b–18c edge also preserves the father-versus-brothers difference and the continuation-only shattering clause. No family-clause equivalence is established.

source_verse.text: He did what was evil before the Lord, though not as his brothers did, nor as his mother did.

target_verses.text: He did what was evil in the eyes of the Lord, though not as his father and not as his mother had done. He removed the pillars of Baal that his father had made.

unresolved_candidates.status: pending proposed accession-synchronism harmonization; no chronology credit
unresolved_candidates.reason: Both complete actual notices identify Ahaziah becoming king in Judah during Joram of Israel’s reign, but8:25 states the twelfth year and9:29 the eleventh. source_verse.text: In the twelfth year of Joram son of Ahab king of Israel, Ahaziah son of Joram became king.

target_verses.text: In the eleventh year of Joram king of Israel, Ahaziah became king over Judah.

unresolved_candidates.status: pending proposed accession-age harmonization; no numerical reconciliation credit
unresolved_candidates.reason: The complete actual Kings notice says twenty-two years old, while the pinned Saints Chronicles notice says twenty years old, not the forty-two found in other editions. The retained partial pair concerns the explicit one-year Jerusalem reign and mother Athaliah daughter of Omri. The age difference remains unresolved.

source_verse.text: Ahaziah was twenty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned one year in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Athaliah, daughter of Omri king of Israel.

target_verses.text: Ahaziah was twenty years old when he became king, and he reigned one year in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Athaliah daughter of Omri.

unresolved_candidates.status: pending proposed Ahaziah accession-synchronism equation; no chronology reconciliation credit
unresolved_candidates.reason: The source announces Ahaziah becoming king in Joram of Israel eleventh year; the earlier Kings notice gives the twelfth year. The retained connection is the explicit named accession only. This reverse-direction review adds no solution or independent reconciliation credit to the already unresolved earlier notice.

source_verse.text: In the eleventh year of Joram king of Israel, Ahaziah became king over Judah.

target_verses.text: In the twelfth year of Joram son of Ahab king of Israel, Ahaziah son of Joram became king.

unresolved_candidates.status: pending proposed identity of financial phases and funds; no financial harmonization credit
unresolved_candidates.reason: Kings forbids making its listed gold or silver temple articles from the collected silver; Chronicles narrates articles made from remaining silver after the work was finished. The supplied restriction and explicitly later remainder are compared as distinct statements. No independent proof equates their complete funding histories or resolves all accounting scope.

source_verse.text: But silver doors, nails, bowls, trumpets, or any gold or silver vessel were not to be made for the Lord’s house from the silver brought into the Lord’s house.

target_verses.text: When they finished, they brought the remaining silver to the king and Jehoiada. They made articles for the Lord’s house: articles for the service of burnt offerings and golden and silver incense vessels. They offered burnt offerings continually in the Lord’s house all Jehoiada’s days.

unresolved_candidates.status: pending proposed killer-name, family-clause, and count harmonization; no identity or numerical reconciliation credit
unresolved_candidates.reason: The retained partial connection is Joash death, David-city burial, and Amaziah succession. Kings names Jezichar son of Jemuath and Jezebuth with the actual his son Shomer phrase. Chronicles names Zabed son of Samath and Jozabed son of Somaroth, adds national descriptions, then all his sons and the five came against him. Those names, relationships, group scope, and counts remain unresolved rather than normalized.

source_verse.text: Jezichar son of Jemuath and Jezebuth—his son Shomer—his slaves, struck him, and he died. They buried him with his fathers in the city of David, and Amaziah his son became king in his place.

target_verses.text: After they left him, leaving him with grave illnesses, his servants attacked him because of the blood of the son of Jehoiada the priest. They put him to death on his bed, and he died. They buried him in David’s city, but did not bury him in the tomb of the kings.
Those who attacked him were Zabed son of Samath, the Ammonite, and Jozabed son of Somaroth, the Moabite,
and all his sons; the five came against him. The remaining matters are written in the writing of the kings. His son Amaziah reigned in his place.

unresolved_candidates.status: pending proposed accession-chronology harmonization; no chronology credit
unresolved_candidates.reason: The retained notices identify Hoshea son of Ela succeeding Phakee and ruling Israel in Samaria, but state twentieth-year Jotham and twelfth-year Ahaz synchronisms. The surrounding Jotham reign notice states sixteen years. The bounded retained pair concerns only the named succession; no independent regnal-calendar or coregency solution is established.

source_verse.text: Hoshea son of Ela formed a conspiracy against Phakee son of Romelias, struck him, put him to death, and became king in his place, in the twentieth year of Jotham son of Azariah.

target_verses.text: In the twelfth year of Ahaz king of Judah, Hoshea son of Ela became king in Samaria over Israel, for nine years.

unresolved_candidates.status: pending proposed clause or identity equivalence; no reconciliation credit
unresolved_candidates.reason: Kings says the eyes were lifted on high against Israel’s Holy One; Isaiah says they were not lifted toward Him. The retained pair compares the explicit reproach, raised voice and named Holy One while preserving both eye clauses; their polarity is not reconciled.

source_verse.text: Whom have you reproached and blasphemed? Against whom have you raised your voice? You have lifted your eyes on high against Israel’s Holy One!

target_verses.text: Whom did you reproach and provoke? Against whom did you raise your voice? Yet you did not lift your eyes on high toward the Holy One of Israel.

unresolved_candidates.status: pending proposed clause or identity equivalence; no reconciliation credit
unresolved_candidates.reason: Kings’s first-year self-growing food and second-year sprouts differ from Isaiah’s first-year what-you-have-sown and second-year what-remains. The retained comparison credits the explicit three-stage sign, third-year sowing, harvest and vineyards, not an agricultural equivalence.

source_verse.text: This shall be the sign for you: You shall eat this year what grows by itself, and in the second year what sprouts. In the third, sowing, harvest, and planting vineyards; you shall eat their fruit.

target_verses.text: This is your sign: This year eat what you have sown, in the second year what remains, and in the third, after sowing, reap and plant vineyards; you will eat their fruit.

source_verse.text: Hezekiah said to Isaiah, ‘What is the sign that the Lord will heal me and I shall go up to the Lord’s house on the third day?’

target_verses.text: Hezekiah said, “This is the sign that I will go up to the house of the Lord God.”

target_verses.text: At that time Marodach son of Laadan, king of Babylonia, sent letters, envoys, and gifts to Hezekiah, for he heard that he had been ill to the point of death and had recovered.

unresolved_candidates.status: pending proposed reconciliation of Josiah death sequence and location; no death-sequence reconciliation credit
unresolved_candidates.reason: Kings states that Nechao killed Josiah at Mageddo when he saw him, and the following Kings unit transports him dead to Jerusalem. Chronicles narrates archers shooting at Josiah, his report of great pain, transport to Jerusalem, and then death. The retained partial connection is the explicit Egyptian Euphrates campaign and Josiah confrontation, while the differing death sequence remains unresolved.

source_verse.text: In his days Pharaoh Nechao king of Egypt went up against the king of the Assyrians to the River Euphrates. Josiah went to meet him, and Nechao killed him at Mageddo when he saw him.

target_verses.text: Pharaoh Neco king of Egypt went up against the king of the Assyrians at the River Euphrates, and King Josiah went to meet him.

He sent messengers to him, saying, “What is there between me and you, king of Judah? I have not come against you today to make war, and God has told me to hurry. Beware of God, who is with me, lest He destroy you.”
Josiah did not turn his face away from him, but strengthened himself to fight him. He did not listen to Neco’s words through God’s mouth, and came to fight in the plain of Magedon.
The archers shot at King Josiah, and the king said to his servants, “Bring me out, for I am in great pain.”
His servants brought him out of the chariot, put him into his second chariot, and brought him to Jerusalem. He died and was buried with his fathers. All Judah and Jerusalem mourned for Josiah,

unresolved_candidates.status: pending proposed tribute-amount harmonization; no numerical reconciliation credit
unresolved_candidates.reason: Both passages supply one hundred talents of silver and Pharaoh removing the Judean king from Jerusalem rule; Kings gives one hundred talents of gold and Chronicles gives one talent of gold. The bounded removal-and-silver correspondence is retained without reconciling the gold amounts.

source_verse.text: Pharaoh Nechao removed him at Deblatha in Emath’s land so that he would not reign in Jerusalem. He imposed a penalty on the land of one hundred talents of silver and one hundred talents of gold.

target_verses.text: Pharaoh Neco bound him at Deblatha in the land of Emath so that he would not reign in Jerusalem,
and the king transported him to Egypt and imposed tribute on the land of one hundred talents of silver and one talent of gold.

unresolved_candidates.status: pending proposed prison-release date and regnal-expression harmonization; no date reconciliation credit
unresolved_candidates.reason: Both passages locate the royal prison release in the thirty-seventh deportation year and twelfth month. Kings gives the twenty-seventh day and in the year of his reign; Jeremiah gives the twenty-fourth day and in the year he became king. The release and shared year/month are retained without equating the day or regnal expressions or independently certifying the name forms.

source_verse.text: In the thirty-seventh year of the deportation of Joakim king of Judah, in the twelfth month, on the twenty-seventh of the month, Euilmarodach king of Babylon, in the year of his reign, lifted the head of Joakim king of Judah and brought him out of his prison house.

target_verses.text: In the thirty-seventh year after Ioakim king of Judah had been deported, in the twelfth month, on the twenty-fourth of the month, Oulaimaradach king of Babylon, in the year he became king, took up the head of Ioakim king of Judah and brought him out of the house where he was guarded.
